scene_translation: Shinjuku Station at dusk — tens of thousands of people flowing like a river. Testo had just passed through the south exit ticket gate, suitcase in hand. And then — a complete stranger, an old man, walked straight toward Testo. "I've been waiting for you, Testo-san. Please take this," the old man said in a quiet voice, holding out a small envelope. Testo had no memory of telling anyone here their name.
grammar_note: 【〜たところだった】means 'had just done ~' — it describes an action that finished only moments before. Here: 改札を出たところだった = 'had just come out of the ticket gate.' The past tense (〜たところだった) is slightly different from the present 〜たところだ, emphasizing that this moment-in-time is now being recalled.

vocab.meaning: to hold out, to extend toward someone

mystery_memo: The central mystery: a stranger at Shinjuku Station south exit knew Testo's name without being told and delivered a small envelope. Contents unknown. The old man's identity and how he knew Testo are the core thread. Old man relationship: neutral/mysterious — no history yet. The envelope is the first key item and must be opened/referenced in a future scene to reveal its first clue.
